title: Mulching: materials, depth and sourcing
audience: Garden maintenance crews and buyers who choose, measure, source, spread and record mulch for garden beds and tree rings.
learningOutcomes: Choose a mulch material that suits the planting, the site and the client's approved scope.
Measure the bed area and calculate the volume needed so that the order is accurate and wasteful over-ordering is avoided.
Spread mulch to the correct depth and keep it away from stems, crowns and trunks.
Check the source and contents of mulch to avoid contamination, weeds and treated timber.

instruction.heading: Why mulch saves time and money
instruction.body: Mulch reduces water loss from soil, suppresses weeds, moderates soil temperature and gives beds a finished look. For a garden maintenance business, mulching is a cost-saving service when it is done well, because it reduces the frequency of weeding and watering that the client pays for later. It can also become a cost problem when the wrong product is used, the bed is measured wrongly, or the material has to be carted away because it is contaminated. This lesson shows you how to plan the volume, choose the material, spread it correctly and avoid the sourcing mistakes that cost money and damage plants.

instruction.heading: Choosing the material
instruction.body: Common mulch materials include wood chip, bark, pine straw or needles, sugarcane mulch, and compost. Each behaves differently. Coarse bark and wood chip break down slowly and suit shrub beds and paths. Fine mulches pack down more easily and can form a crust that repels water. Compost is a soil improver as well as a mulch, but it can carry weed seed and may need a different depth. Choose the material by its suitability for the planting and the site. Consider the slope, wind, fire-prone areas and whether the bed is near a path or a boundary where material can wash out. Ask the client whether they have preferences, but do not recommend a material that the business is not able to source in a way it can document.

instruction.heading: Measuring, calculating and ordering
instruction.body: Measure each bed in square metres. For a rectangle, multiply length by width. For an irregular bed, divide it into simple shapes, measure each, and add them together. Subtract the area of permanent structures such as paving, tree trunks and garden ornaments. Multiply the area by the planned depth to find the volume. Convert the volume into the units the supplier sells, and add a small allowance for settling and waste, not a large one. Order in bulk where the site and delivery make it economical, and check the delivery access and the drop-off point before ordering. A mulch order that is too large leaves material to be disposed of, which is an extra cost and a waste-handling task. A mulch order that is too small leaves a patchy finish and forces a second trip. Record the measurements, the volume and the order in the job sheet.

instruction.heading: Spreading to the right depth
instruction.body: Spread mulch evenly and to the depth set by the product guidance and the planting needs. Keep mulch away from the stems and crowns of plants and away from the base of trees, where it can cause rot and attract pests. Pull mulch back from the trunk so there is a clear ring around it. Rake the surface level and check that no mulch has fallen onto paths, lawns or drains. Water the bed if the client expects it, and tell the client how the material will settle over the following weeks. Do not bury plants or cover the crown of a shrub, because that can kill it.

instruction.heading: Source checks and contamination
instruction.body: Check where the mulch comes from before it arrives. Ask the supplier for the product description and its source, and keep the supplier's documentation with the job record. Watch for weeds and invasive plants in the material, including seeds, runners and fragments. Do not use mulch that has visible weed growth, mould or an unusual smell. Keep any contaminated load separate and do not spread it. Where the material contains an invasive plant, follow the biosecurity lesson and refer the decision. Do not claim that a mulch is free of weeds, chemicals or contamination unless the supplier's evidence supports the claim.

instruction.heading: Verification and records
instruction.body: A supervisor should check the measurement, the material and the finish. A competent worker can show how they calculated the area and volume, explain why they chose the material, point to the source documentation, identify a contaminated load and describe how a bed should look when the mulch is pulled back from the stems. Records should show what was ordered, what was delivered, what was spread and where any load was referred. Escalate any load with treated timber, weeds, mould or unknown material, and any request to mulch over plant crowns or into a restricted area.

procedure: Measure each bed, subtract permanent structures, and calculate the area in square metres.
Choose a mulch material suited to the planting, the site and the approved scope.
Calculate the volume at the planned depth, add a modest allowance, and convert to the supplier's units.
Check the delivery access and drop-off point, then confirm the order and the delivery date in writing.
On arrival, check the material for weeds, treated timber, mould and unusual smell, and reject any contaminated load.
Clear the bed of old debris and weeds, and keep stems and trunks free of mulch.
Spread the mulch evenly to the planned depth, and pull it back from stems, crowns and trunks.
Rake the surface level, clear mulch from paths and drains, and record the volume used and the client sign-off.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a shrub bed to be mulched. The bed is irregular, with a tree trunk in one corner and a paved path along one edge. The client wants the bed filled to the top of the edging.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you measure, order and spread the mulch?
workedExamples.reasoning: Measure the bed in sections, subtract the area of the trunk and the path, and calculate the volume at the planned depth. Add a modest allowance and order with the supplier, checking the delivery drop-off. Spread the mulch evenly, keep it clear of the trunk and any shrub crowns, and sweep any spill off the path. If the client wants the bed filled to the top of the edging without regard to plant crowns, explain the risk and record the decision.

workedExamples.situation: A delivery of mulch arrives with pieces of painted timber and a few seedlings of a plant the crew cannot identify.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the load?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not spread the mulch. Keep the load separate and inform the supervisor. Painted timber may be treated or contaminated, and unidentified seedlings may be invasive. Record the load, photograph it with consent, and contact the supplier to confirm the product and to arrange a replacement or return. Follow the biosecurity lesson for the seedlings and the waste lesson for disposal.

equipmentAndPpe: Calculator or job sheet template for volume
Gloves suitable for handling wood and bark
Eye protection for spreading and raking
Dust mask where fine mulch is dusty, selected for the hazard
Tarps for protecting paths and lawns during spreading

commonErrors.error: Ordering the volume from the rough area without subtracting paths, trunks or structures.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure each bed in sections, subtract permanent structures and calculate the volume at the planned depth.

commonErrors.error: Piling mulch against stems, crowns or trunks.
commonErrors.prevention: Pull mulch back from every stem and trunk and keep a clear ring around each plant.

commonErrors.error: Spreading a load with visible weeds, treated timber or mould.
commonErrors.prevention: Check every load on arrival, keep any suspect load separate and refer it before spreading.

commonErrors.error: Telling the client the mulch is weed-free or chemical-free without evidence.
commonErrors.prevention: State only what the supplier's documentation supports, and record the source.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Mulch and organic material may carry plant pests, weeds and invasive species, and movement and disposal rules are set by each state and territory.
Under general horticultural practice, treated timber should not be used in garden beds.
Lifting and spreading bulk mulch is a manual-handling task. Use mechanical aids and manual-handling controls to reduce strain.

qualityStandard: Each bed's area and volume are calculated and recorded before ordering.
Every load is checked on arrival, and suspect loads are kept separate and referred.
Mulch is spread to the planned depth, and no mulch is against stems, crowns or trunks.
Paths, lawns and drains are clear of mulch at the end of the job.
documentationEvidence: Measurement and volume calculation for each bed, with the material chosen and the order reference.
Supplier documentation for the product, including its source.
Delivery check record, including any rejected or referred load.
Volume used and client sign-off for the completed bed.
summary: Measure each bed carefully, subtract structures, and order the volume you need with a modest allowance.
Choose the material for the planting and the site, and document its source.
Check every delivery for weeds, treated timber and mould before spreading.
Spread to the planned depth and keep mulch away from stems, crowns and trunks.

knowledgeChecks.question: A bed is 6 metres by 3 metres with a 1 square metre tree ring and a 2 square metre paved corner. What is the planting area for mulch volume?
options: 18 square metres, because the full rectangle is mulched.
15 square metres, after subtracting the tree ring and the paved corner.
1 square metre, because only the open soil is counted.

knowledgeChecks.question: On arrival a mulch delivery contains painted timber and unknown seedlings. What is the correct action?
options: Spread it quickly, since the timber is small, the seedlings are few, and the client is waiting for the mulch to go down today.
Bury the painted timber under the mulch so it cannot be seen by the client or the neighbours on the day of the delivery.
Keep the load separate, record it, contact the supplier and refer the seedlings and timber under the relevant procedures.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should mulch be placed around a shrub?
options: Pulled back from the stem and crown, leaving a clear ring around the plant.
Piled against the stem and over the crown to protect the roots.
Packed tightly around the trunk so the plant is held upright.
